page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by Intel Xeon 8559C processors. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 320 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

This server includes 120,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, designed for high-capacity and low-latency data access. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs are included in this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the i7ie.metal-48xl demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core tests, Passmark CPU scores, and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, achieving top-tier results in both cached small-block and uncached large-block read/write operations. Database performance is a key strength, with Redis SET operations reaching 214.78 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring in the top 10%. Single-core performance, however, sits in the average tier.

Given its massive local storage capacity and high memory density, this bare-metal instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive deployments that would otherwise require multi-node clustering. It is optimized for large-scale databases, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation, and CPU-based LLM inference.
